name: Ben-ammi
overview: Ben-ammi is a male figure identified as the son of Lot and the forebear of the Ammonite tribe. He is distinguished by his unique role as an ancestor to the Ammonites, a people descended from him, as recorded in Genesis 19:38. No additional notes are provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Ben-ammi means 'son of my people,' reflecting his origin and relationship to the Ammonite people. Another related name, Ammon, means 'my people,' highlighting the tribal identity that stems from him. Neither name is indicated as being given by God, but both carry significance in identifying his lineage and tribal affiliation.
familyAndRelationships: Ben-ammi is explicitly recorded as the son of Lot, also referred to as the younger of Lot, establishing his immediate family connection. Additionally, he is inferred as an ancestor to Nahash and Zelek, linking him genealogically to later figures associated with the Ammonites. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Ben-ammi's significance lies primarily in his role as the progenitor of the Ammonite people, an important tribal group in the biblical narrative. His descent from Lot connects the Ammonites to the broader story of Israel's neighbors. As an ancestor figure, he provides a genealogical foundation that helps explain the origins of the Ammonite nation and its place in biblical history.
